educationalGoal: A distributed system is a technology for integrating both computers and networks, and is an attempt to link computers that originally operated independently to a network. In this class, we will focus on computer architecture, processes, client-server, communication, naming, clock and synchronization, fault-tolerance, and security, which are necessary for learning distributed systems.

achievementLevels.ideal:
Within 15 weeks you will be able to
1. Analyze the technical advantages of specific developments in distributed computer systems.
2. Demonstrate system analysis using existing scientific and engineering knowledge.
3. Further develop an attitude that allows them to explain problems clearly. Improve the quality of feedback.
4. Clearly summarize the analysis in a presentation or report.
5. Evaluate the demonstrated analysis of others.
achievementLevels.standard:
Within 15 weeks you will be able to

1. Explain the technical advantages in the field of distributed systems.
2. Explain how to analyze a system using existing scientific and engineering knowledge.
3. Be able to clearly explain the problem.
4. Be able to summarize the analysis in a presentation or report.
5. Be able to understand the demonstrated analysis of others.

lessons.content:
1. Overview of distributed systems
I will take up what a distributed system is and
explain some of its advantages over a
centralized system.

2. Types of distributed systems
Understand the types and purposes of
distributed systems. Learn what is different
about how each type of configuration.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 2 of Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 3 of the
textbook)

lessons.content:
3. Communication
Learn about basic reference models and basic
functions for exchanging data between
components of a distributed system.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 3 of Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 4 of the
textbook)

lessons.content:
4. Naming
Explain common naming issues in distributed
systems and learn about the main methods of
naming.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 4 of Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 5 of the
textbook)

lessons.content:
5. Architecture
Learn basic design and concepts such as the
design philosophy and basic design of
distributed systems.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 5 of Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 6 of the
textbook)

lessons.content:
6. Process
Learn about the execution units in a
distributed system such as “process” and
“thread”.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 6 of Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 7 of the
textbook)

lessons.content:
7. Client-Server model
Learn the classification and characteristics of
both clients and servers from several
perspectives.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 7 of Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 8 of the
textbook)

lessons.content:
8. Clock and Synchronization
Learn about the basic methods of clock
synchronization and the exclusive control
algorithms in distributed systems.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 8 of Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 9 of the
textbook)

lessons.content:
9. Fault Torrent
Learn about basic concepts and techniques for
introducing fault tolerance into distributed
systems.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 9 of Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 10 of
the textbook)

lessons.content:
10. Network Security
Learn about cryptographic technologies,
authentication technologies, communication
methods, and access control.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 10 of
Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 11 of
the textbook)

lessons.content:
11. Distributed files and objects
Learn the advantages and disadvantages of
distributed files compared to centralized file
systems.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 11 of
Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 12 of
the textbook)

lessons.content:
12. Distributed web systems
Learn about the characteristics of distributed
web systems for processing a great deal of data.
lessons.assignments:
Review (Chapter 12 of
Textbook)
Preparation (Chapter 13 of
the textbook)

lessons.content:
Hold a lecture on distributed systems with
external lecturers.
